issues.legal_issue: A court may refuse a proposed amendment introducing an apparently time-barred claim when the applicant has shown prolonged negligent delay and given no reasonable explanation for it.
material_facts: The proceeding began as an eviction suit and was converted into a title suit after the defendant asserted a rival title based on a sale deed.
The defendant’s rival title was disclosed in the pleadings many years before the amendment application, and the court had earlier allowed the plaintiffs an opportunity to amend their pleadings.

The plaintiffs did not challenge the sale deed until more than fifteen years after the rival title was asserted; subsequent purchasers also waited several years after acquiring the property before joining the suit.
The amendment application gave no explanation for the delay and sought to introduce a claim that was apparently barred by limitation.
issues.conclusion: The appeal was allowed, the orders permitting amendment were set aside, and the amendment application was dismissed.
issues.legal_principle: Under Order 6 Rule 17 of the Code of Civil Procedure, an amendment may be allowed at any stage, and the fact that a fresh suit on the amended claim would be barred by limitation is a factor in the court’s discretion, not an absolute bar. However, an apparently time-barred claim should not be introduced without a valid basis, bona fides, and a reasonable explanation for delay, particularly where the amendment would defeat rights accrued to the opposing party through lapse of time. The Court relied on Dondapati Narayana Reddy v. Duggireddy Venkatanarayan Reddy and Others, T.N. Alloy Foundry Co. Ltd. v. T.N. Electricity Board and Others, and L.J. Leach & Co. Ltd. v. Jardine Skinner and Co.

rule.if: civil_suit_amendment_application and proposed_claim_apparently_time_barred and (earlier_opportunity_to_amend or rival_title_disclosed_early) and prolonged_unexplained_delay

predicates.civil_suit_amendment_application: A party applied to amend pleadings in a civil suit.
predicates.proposed_claim_apparently_time_barred: The proposed amendment introduced a claim that appeared to be barred by limitation.
predicates.earlier_opportunity_to_amend: The applicant had an earlier opportunity to amend the pleadings but did not use it to raise the proposed claim.
predicates.rival_title_disclosed_early: The opposing party asserted a rival title sufficiently early for the applicant to address it in the pleadings.
predicates.prolonged_unexplained_delay: The applicant waited a prolonged period to seek the amendment and gave no reasonable explanation for the delay.

issues.definition: When a civil suit amendment application introduces an apparently time-barred claim after an earlier opportunity or early disclosure of rival title, and the applicant has caused prolonged unexplained delay, the application is denied.
